Vocal interactions timing analysis

get_vocal_interactions_timing.Rd

Carries out the analysis described in Demartsev et al. 2024 (doi: 10.1098/rstb.2023.0188) #It works as follows: Make a table of all calls within a given call category (set of calls), identify the one who gave the call as the 'caller' For each call, identify all other individuals ('responders') who were present (calls labeled) on that day Also identify the distance between the caller and responder at the time when the call was given by the caller (if desired) Save this table as callresp Note: This table DOES include self-responses (which can be useful for looking at self-response patterns, or can be filtered out later) Then for each of row in this table, look at the call sequence of the 'responder' over time, lined up so that t = 0 = time of the 'caller' call Run a kernel over this time series to smooth it with a bandwidth bw = .1 sec (or as specified by parameters bw) Save the output to a matrix as callresp_seqs, such that the indices in the table match the indices in the matrix In subsequent code, these sequences can be further explored and plotted. For instance, we can get the mean across all (or a subset) of rows of the matrix for different conditions: Different distance bins (aggregate only data from caller-responder pairs within a range of distances from one another) Different age/sex/dominance classes (aggregate only data from caller-responder pairs where the caller was a certain status, and the responder was a certain status) Investigate self-interactions Etc. callresp_table: data frame of call-response pairs w/ relevant columns caller: str id of the calling individual whose call triggers the sequence (lined up at t = 0) responder: str id of the responding individual whose subsequent calls are being monitored t0: numeric time of the caller call in POSIXct form tf: numeric time of the caller call in POSIXct form distance: numeric distance between caller and responder at the time of the original call a few other columns used in processing callresp.seqs: matrix of call-response sequences, where each row represents the sequence associated with each row in the callresp data frame and each column represents a point in time tseq: vector giving the time point associated with the columns of callresp_seqs (in seconds)

Usage

get_vocal_interactions_timing(
  calls,
  caller_calltype,
  responder_calltype,
  bw = 0.1,
  step = 0.02,
  max_lag = 3,
  trigger_on = "begin",
  xs = NULL,
  ys = NULL,
  timestamps = NULL,
  audioOn = NULL
)

Arguments

calls

data frame of calls, with columns call_type (call type, character string), t0 (start time in POSIXct UTC), tf (end time in POSIXct UTC), ind_idx (individual index, matching to rows in xs and ys matrices if present), and optionally time_idx (index of closest time point that matches to timestamps vector)

bw

bandwidth of the kernel to use in the analysis

step

time resolution (in sec)

max_lag

max time lag to consider (in sec)

trigger_on

string specifying if you should trigger on the beginning of calls ('begin') or end of calls ('end')

xs

N x n_times matrix of eastings for all individuals

ys

N x n_times matrix of northings for all individuals

timestamps

vector of POSIXct (UTC) timestamps corresponding to columns in xs and ys

audioOn

N x n_times matrix of whether each individual has audio data at each second (T or F)

caller_calltypes

string giving a regular expression for what initiator (focal) call types to include

responder_calltypes

string giving a regular expression for what repsonder call types to include

Value

Returns a list containing: callresp: the table of callers, responders, call times, distances, etc. callresp_seqs: vocal sequence of the responder relative to the time of the caller's call out$tseq: time sequence used (maps to the columns of callresp_seqs) out$callresp_means_all: mean across the columns of callresp_seqs - the average response to a call (across all data, including self responses) out$callresp_means_other: mean across the columns of callresp_seqs - the average response to a call including only non-self responses, i.e. responses to others individuals) out$callresp_means_self: mean across the columnns of callresp_seqs - the average response to a call including only self-responses), i.e. the typical time between calls in a single individual's vocal sequence
